text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Secretary of State for the Budget, Manuela Arcanjo says there will be no tax rises in 1997. Manuela Arcanjo said public investment and exports will boost the economy in 1997.
- State water company EPAL - Empresa Portuguesa das Aguas Livres - registered 1.4 billion escudo profit in the first half of 1996.
- The judicial year starts today and promises to be highly controversial with many important public personalities involved in criminal cases.

- Portugal may have to pay 80 billion escudos in fines if it does not respect the three percent of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for the budget deficit, after the creation of the European Monetary Union.
- Cement company Cimpor is the most profitable in the market. Chairman Antonio Sousa Gomes expects foreign investors to participate in its privatisation.

- More than five thousand workers will lose their jobs if the Government closes several mines. Secretary of State for the Industry and Energy, Jose Penedos, says it was a mistake for the state to interfer in the industrial sector.
